questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Course selection and academic level

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have given my stay a full 10/10 if i have had a better living experience (i'll elaborate later.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The website is easy to navigate.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of helpful email from the International Office in Heidelberg.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I just signed up at the Studierendenwerk Heidelberg, when i received the email from them and they offered me a dorm room in the first round because i was a 4EU+ student.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's cheap, but it's nothing like the social dorm in Copenhagen. Quite the opposite actually. I've never had a full conversation with either of my three roommates. If your looking for a social place to live, find a WG on your own in the city!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I wouldn't recommend living at Ilse-Krall-Str. to anybody!!! Because:
1. You are allowed to smoke inside and since the person beneath me smooked my room smelled like cigarets 24/7
2. As a woman i didn't feel same in the neighborhood, because people would catcall all the time the first 2 months
3. Even though i isn't so far out of the city on a map, it just feels so out of nowhere compared to how small Heidelberg is
4. Absolutely no social life

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just do what you are told in the emails and on Mobility Online and everything will go smoothly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got sent an email from the International Office, completed the steps in Mobility Online and received my login and student number so i could acces the services, platforms and portals at the university. Easy!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office in Heidelberg was very helpfull and has helped though everything during my exchange. They are the best and i never felt stupid to ask anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the 4 classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I registred via LSF with my login, but the most common thing is actually just to write the professor an email and show up on the first day of class. That's what almost all the german students do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Heidelberg University is a highly ranked uni and you can really feel it!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Since all of my classes existed of exclusively german people and then me, the academic level was really good and motivational. In the beginning i did experience som difficulties language-wise though, but i caught up to it quickly, because people was so patient and helpfull

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Everything is so formal in german. You get called Frau/Herr + Lastname and they use the formal Sie about you. But the professers at the Institut Deutsch als Fremdsprache are all so nice, professional and welcoming, so it wasn't a problem to be a little extra formal. Even though if was very different for me and my UCPH chilled vibe.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Daf-Unterricht, 10 ects
2. Bildungssprache, 6 ects
3. Theorien der Fremdsprachendidaktik, 4 ects
4. Verfahren der Sprachstandsmessung (Diagnostik), 6 ects

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: DaF-Unterricht and Diagnostik were both so practical and useful for those who study to become a teacher. 10/10 would recommend both courses!

questions.answer: Everything is cheaper here, so don't bring hair, skin etc. product. Save the space to something else

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Try to sign up for the uni sports and excursions when they get launched!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many things, but a lot of them got filled very quickly. Fx uni sports and excursions

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Uni sports, excursions arranged by the uni, ESN social gatherings/parties, Boho Club at mondays and the Buddy Programme

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Cities: Speyer, Schwarzwald, Freibung, Mannheim and München
Go to the Strandbad Waisee on a hot day and not the Fribäder. It's the best place to swim and not crowded.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. People are so friendly and helpfull

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If a group of international students approached you and your friends in Copenhagen and invited you go grab a coffee, would you be rude and turn them down? No, so keep that in mind when you go on exchange.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The political view on certain things, fx climate and queerness. I would say it was challenging, more like interesting and eyeopening. Especially when talking to international student, who came from countries i didn't know so much about. I definitely had some eye opening talks during my exchange.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness all over!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Bring a USB for printing out administrative form. Germany handles everything in paper, so be prepared for the old fashioned bureaucracy
2. If you're doing an exchange in the summer period, bring MAX 1 sweater. The cold weather will turn into 25 degrees in no time!!
3. Speak german as much as you can, it will benefite you in so many ways both academically, professionally and socially

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't mind people staring lol. That's apparently very normal in Heidelberg. Rent a Swapfiets! And safe some money for traveling around southern Europe with train. You won't believe how close Heidelberg is to everything!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning so much about other cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier sometimes and sticking to speak german 24/7

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Chose to go on exchange with 4EU+. You will get so many advantages that you'll never get with the regular Erasmus exchange programme!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
